nutshell: A relief rally driven by easing geopolitical tensions with Iran.

scripts.speaker: 진행자
scripts.text: This is the closing bell briefing for March 24th. After last week's downturn, all the major indexes finished sharply higher today.

scripts.speaker: 해설자
scripts.text: That's right. Today's market can be summed up in one phrase: a relief rally on easing geopolitical tensions with Iran. The Dow Jones Industrial Average closed up 1.38% at 46,208.47, and the S&P 500 also gained 1.15% to finish at 6,581. The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite jumped 1.38% as well, closing at 21,946.76. War fears that peaked over the weekend dramatically subsided after President Trump mentioned the possibility of dialogue, leading to a rapid recovery in investor sentiment.

sources.title: Stock market today: Dow, S&P 500, Nasdaq soar as Trump postpones Iran strike, citing 'very good' talks

scripts.speaker: 진행자
scripts.text: That's a complete turnaround. Just last Friday, the mood was pessimistic with the market posting its fourth straight week of losses.

scripts.speaker: 해설자
scripts.text: Exactly. When President Trump issued an ultimatum, suggesting military action was on the table in response to Iran's blockade of the Strait of Hormuz, the market was gripped by fears of stagflation. But today, news that he postponed military action and initiated productive talks led the market to believe the biggest uncertainty had been resolved. This shift was crystal clear in oil prices, where West Texas Intermediate crude plunged nearly 10% to the $88 level as supply disruption fears eased.

sources.title: Stock market today: Dow, S&P 500, Nasdaq futures fall as 4-week down spiral continues, Trump threatens Iran

scripts.speaker: 진행자
scripts.text: So, could you break down the key drivers that moved the market today?

scripts.speaker: 해설자
scripts.text: Yes, we can really break it down into two main themes. First, the relief rally triggered by de-escalating geopolitical tensions, and second, the return of risk-on sentiment, best seen in plunging oil prices and soaring stocks. We'll dig into each of these in just a moment.

scripts.speaker: 진행자
scripts.text: Alright, let's start with that first point: the relief rally sparked by easing geopolitical tensions. How exactly did different assets move?

scripts.speaker: 해설자
scripts.text: Right. Today we saw a 'great unwind' across all asset classes, reversing the war fears from last week. President Trump's mention of dialogue significantly lowered the odds of the worst-case scenario—a blockade of the Strait of Hormuz—which triggered a mass unwinding of risk-off positions. While the S&P 500 climbed over 1%, the VIX, the market's fear gauge, plummeted more than 10% to the 26 level. The most dramatic moves were in commodities. WTI crude, with supply fears evaporating, plunged nearly 10% to close around $89 a barrel. Gold, a classic safe-haven, also retreated to the $4,400 an ounce level. In the bond market, we saw a typical risk-on move as well, with the 10-year Treasury yield rising slightly to around 4.33% as safe-haven demand weakened.

scripts.speaker: 진행자
scripts.text: Those moves in assets like oil and gold are pretty striking. So within the stock market, which sectors were most affected? I imagine we saw the opposite of last week's trends.

scripts.speaker: 해설자
scripts.text: You're spot on. The winners and losers from last week completely flipped roles overnight. With the likelihood of conflict decreasing, defense stocks like Lockheed Martin and RTX all saw a pullback, and the related ETF, XAR, closed slightly lower, giving back some of its recent war premium. On the flip side, the biggest beneficiaries were airline and travel-related stocks. The combination of reduced geopolitical risk and a sharp drop in oil prices—a major cost component—acted as a double tailwind. The airline-focused ETF, JETS, along with related stocks, showed strong upward momentum. So the market reacted instantly to the Iran news, creating a clear divergence among sectors.

sources.title: Defense Stocks Retreat, Airlines Soar as De-escalation Sparks Sector Rotation
Trump Backs Off From Iran Threat as Ceasefire Talks Get Underway

scripts.speaker: 진행자
scripts.text: It sounds like the Iran issue explains everything. Did any of the economic data released today have much of an impact on the market?

scripts.speaker: 해설자
scripts.text: The geopolitical news was so dominant that other data took a backseat, but actually, the economic reports today helped support the relief rally. The preliminary March Manufacturing PMI from S&P Global came in at 51.0, beating expectations of 50.2. The Services PMI also topped forecasts at 51.7, versus an expected 50.4, showing that economic expansion remains solid. This signaled to investors that, aside from the wildcard of the Iran risk, the fundamentals of the U.S. economy are still strong. It gave them the confidence to jump back into stocks aggressively once that uncertainty was removed. The stable performance of the Dollar Index can also be seen as a reflection of this confidence in the fundamentals.

scripts.speaker: 진행자
scripts.text: So, it seems the geopolitical risk has lifted for now, and we've got confirmation that the economic fundamentals are solid. The question is, can this relief rally continue? And what will the market be watching next?

scripts.speaker: 해설자
scripts.text: While the relief could continue in the short term, it's crucial to remember this situation has been 'postponed,' not resolved. Tensions could flare up again at any moment if talks break down, so geopolitical risk will remain a backdrop for the market. Because of that, the market's focus is likely to shift quickly back to the economy's fundamental drivers: the Federal Reserve's monetary policy and key economic indicators. Traders will be looking to reassess the economic picture with data like next week's non-farm payrolls report. The direction of bond yields will also reflect market expectations for the Fed's policy path. Ultimately, this rally is largely a technical bounce on relief that the worst-case scenario was avoided. For it to become a sustained uptrend, we'll need confirmation from the key variables: the economy, inflation, and Fed policy.

scripts.speaker: 진행자
scripts.text: As you said, the risk isn't completely gone. But today's market clearly showed a return to risk-on sentiment, with oil plunging and stocks surging. Could you analyze that trend in more detail?

scripts.speaker: 해설자
scripts.text: Yes, as the worst-case scenario that weighed on the market all weekend vanished, all assets breathed a collective sigh of relief. The Dow Jones Industrial Average jumped 1.38%, the S&P 500 gained 1.15%, and the Nasdaq surged 1.38%, all staging a powerful rebound. The catalyst for all this was President Trump's announcement that he was postponing military action and had started productive talks with Iran. The most sensitive asset, West Texas Intermediate crude, reacted by plunging over 9.5% to settle around $88 a barrel. What's interesting is that even as risk appetite for assets like stocks increased, the 10-year U.S. Treasury yield actually fell by more than 5 basis points to 4.33%, helped by easing inflation expectations due to the oil price drop. The U.S. dollar, a safe-haven asset, also weakened by about 0.5%. As the stagflation fears that had been gripping the market faded, we saw an unusual phenomenon where both stocks and bonds rallied at the same time.

Stock market today: Dow jumps 600 points, S&P 500, Nasdaq surge as Trump signals talks with Iran; oil tumbles

scripts.speaker: 진행자
scripts.text: I'd imagine the drop in oil prices created a clear divide between winning and losing sectors. How did things look on a sector-by-sector basis?

scripts.speaker: 해설자
scripts.text: Yes, as expected, the biggest beneficiaries of the oil drop were the airlines. Since fuel is such a huge component of their costs, the plunge in oil was an immediate tailwind. The U.S. Global Jets ETF (JETS) rose nearly 3.5%, with American Airlines and Delta Air Lines leading the charge, up 3.6% and 2.7% respectively. The energy sector, on the other hand, showed a more interesting dynamic. While oil majors like ExxonMobil and Chevron initially dropped sharply on the WTI price collapse, they managed to erase all their losses and actually finish higher, lifted by the powerful buying sentiment across the broader market. The Energy Select Sector SPDR Fund (XLE) also recovered from its intraday losses to close up 0.5%. This suggests that the macro tailwind from easing geopolitical risk was strong enough to overpower the short-term headwind for that specific sector.

scripts.speaker: 진행자
scripts.text: I'm also curious about the impact on macroeconomic data. There were some economic reports out today, but did the market only react to the geopolitical news?

scripts.speaker: 해설자
scripts.text: That's right. Today's rally was a classic case of a geopolitical factor overwhelming everything else. Coincidentally, the economic data released today was actually quite weak, with all reports missing market expectations. The Chicago Fed National Activity Index for March came in at negative 0.11, well below the positive reading that was expected, signaling a slowdown. Construction spending also showed unexpected weakness, falling 0.3% month-over-month. Normally, news like this would spark recession fears, but the market completely ignored it. In fact, some may have interpreted the weak data as a positive, as the sharp drop in oil prices eased inflation pressures, giving the Federal Reserve more room to maneuver. The poor economic numbers might have even fueled hopes for an earlier rate cut.

scripts.speaker: 진행자
scripts.text: The market mood has shifted dramatically in just one day. Can this relief rally be sustained?

scripts.speaker: 해설자
scripts.text: It's too early to say for sure. This rally is hanging on a single catalyst: President Trump's comments. In fact, Iran's foreign ministry has created some confusion by denying that any talks with the U.S. have taken place. Experts like Rebecca Babin, a senior energy trader at CIBC Private Wealth, are warning that uncertainty will remain until passage through the Strait of Hormuz is fully normalized. Ian Bremmer, president of Eurasia Group, also believes that short-term shipping disruptions in the strait are likely to continue. So, while the market has breathed a sigh of relief, the root cause of the conflict hasn't been resolved. Investors will be watching the negotiation process closely while shifting their focus back to fundamentals and economic data.

scripts.speaker: 진행자
scripts.text: Right, as you mentioned, the market's focus is shifting back to individual company fundamentals. And in that context, one company that made a notable move today was Freeport-McMoRan. It fell to around $53 early in the session before staging a strong rebound to close up 1.25%. What was behind that move?

scripts.speaker: 해설자
scripts.text: Yes, there's a growing view in the market that sees Freeport-McMoRan not just as a copper miner, but as a key beneficiary of the massive paradigms of AI data centers and the energy transition. The narrative that AI infrastructure requires significantly more copper is gaining traction, and the expectation that Freeport is at the center of this structural demand growth seems to have fueled today's V-shaped recovery in the stock. The strong buying that came in at the intraday low can be seen as the market's positive reaction to this long-term growth story.

scripts.speaker: 진행자
scripts.text: That's a pretty compelling thesis—being the key hardware for AI infrastructure. But we have to ask if this growth expectation lines up with the company's actual financial health.

scripts.speaker: 해설자
scripts.text: And that's exactly where a cautious approach is needed. If you look at their annual report filed in February 2026, the company's financial picture might be different than it appears. While they generated about $5.6 billion in operating cash flow in 2025, a massive capital expenditure of $4.5 billion meant their free cash flow—the cash the company can actually use—was only around $1.1 billion. When you compare the current market cap to that free cash flow, you get a very high valuation of over 70 times. That's a figure that can only be justified by assuming that historically high copper prices will be sustained indefinitely.

scripts.speaker: 진행자
scripts.text: So you're saying the valuation looks stretched. Are there any other risk factors investors should be aware of?

scripts.speaker: 해설자
scripts.text: The most critical risk is its heavy reliance on Indonesia. A staggering 60% of the company's entire pre-tax income comes from a single mine in Indonesia, the Grasberg mine. This mine recently suffered an 'unprecedented mud rush' accident that killed seven people, raising concerns about operational stability, and it's expected to have a significant impact on 2026 results. A bigger problem is regulatory uncertainty with the Indonesian government. A recently introduced rule requiring 100% of export proceeds to be deposited in local banks is a serious constraint on the company's cash flow. Most concerning of all is the fact that the company explicitly states in its annual report that it does not maintain 'political risk insurance' to cover these geopolitical risks.

scripts.speaker: 진행자
scripts.text: So to sum it up, we have a powerful AI growth story on one side, but on the other, a stretched valuation and serious risks concentrated in one specific region.

scripts.speaker: 해설자
scripts.text: Exactly. The current stock performance appears to be focused on the future potential of AI-driven copper demand, while not fully pricing in the real-world risks that could determine the company's fate, like geopolitical issues in Indonesia and commodity price volatility. If copper prices were to revert to their historical average or if further operational disruptions occur in Indonesia, the current high valuation could be difficult to justify. Therefore, rather than focusing solely on the exciting growth narrative, this seems to be a time when careful risk management and a close examination of the company's fundamental risks are warranted.

scripts.speaker: 진행자
scripts.text: It seems hard to sum up today's market in a single word. Could you recap the closing situation for us and highlight what we should be watching going forward?

scripts.speaker: 해설자
scripts.text: Yes, 'mixed' is probably the best word for today's session. The PMI data from S&P Global sent conflicting signals, which made the market's direction ambiguous. While the Manufacturing PMI showed a positive picture by remaining in expansion territory, the Services PMI unexpectedly contracted, fueling concerns about a potential economic slowdown. With this kind of conflicting data, investors found it difficult to get a clear read on the Fed's next move, and as a result, the major indexes fluctuated without a clear direction before closing mixed.

scripts.speaker: 진행자
scripts.text: As you said, the economic indicators seem to be telling different stories. So what should we be keeping an eye on in the coming days?

scripts.speaker: 해설자
scripts.text: Yes, for the time being, the market is likely to react more sensitively to each new piece of economic data as it tries to find its footing. First up, we should watch the weekly initial jobless claims report on Thursday. With many analysts pointing to the strong labor market as a source of inflationary pressure, this report will give us a read on whether the job market is cooling down or still running hot. The market is expecting a slight increase to 210,000 from the previous 205,000, and any significant deviation from that forecast could increase market volatility.

scripts.speaker: 진행자
scripts.text: So that's a key indicator for the temperature of the labor market. Is there any data scheduled that gives us a look into consumer sentiment?

scripts.speaker: 해설자
scripts.text: Absolutely. On Friday, we'll get the final reading of the University of Michigan Consumer Sentiment index. This report is important because it provides clues about consumers' future inflation expectations. If inflation expectations remain elevated, it could lead to concerns that the Fed's tightening cycle might last longer. Looking a bit further out, the most critical report will be the Personal Consumption Expenditures, or PCE, price index, due early next month. Since PCE is the Fed's preferred inflation gauge, its outcome could determine the future path of interest rate policy. Investors are likely to remain in a wait-and-see mode until that key report is released.

scripts.speaker: 진행자
scripts.text: So it all comes back to the Fed's rate decisions. Finally, do you have any closing thoughts for our listeners?

scripts.speaker: 해설자
scripts.text: Right now, the market is like walking through fog. We have a mix of positive and negative signals, so making bold predictions is unwise. In times like these, instead of getting caught up in short-term volatility, it's important to calmly assess the key employment and inflation data as it comes out and try to read the broader market trend. While there's a general consensus that the Fed is nearing the end of its rate-hiking cycle, uncertainty about the pace and the terminal rate remains. Therefore, it's wise to be prepared for increased volatility around key data releases and to approach the market with a more cautious strategy.

scripts.speaker: 진행자
scripts.text: Alright, a cautious approach is needed. Thank you for that analysis. That concludes our closing bell briefing for March 24th. Thanks for listening.
